reference.title: WHO 5th Wilms tumour — COG vs SIOP risk groups & anaplasia criteria
reference.intro: Anaplasia requires ALL three criteria: (1) multipolar polyploid mitotic figures, (2) marked nuclear enlargement (>= 3x adjacent nuclei of same lineage), and (3) hyperchromasia. Tumour rupture/spillage, positive margins, or regional lymph node metastasis automatically upgrades to Stage III.
reference.note: Photomicrographs are from Wikimedia Commons under open Creative Commons licences. ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: COG vs SIOP stratification & adverse molecular markers
points: Focal anaplasia: sharply circumscribed anaplastic focus confined within the primary tumour without nuclear unrest elsewhere and without anaplasia in vessels/extratumoural sites. Any other pattern = diffuse anaplasia.
SIOP post-chemotherapy high-risk: blastemal-predominant (> 66% viable tumour is blastema with < 66% chemotherapy-induced necrosis) or diffuse anaplasia; low-risk: completely necrotic.

Adverse biomarkers: combined LOH at 1p and 16q, 1q gain, and TP53 mutation (strongly linked to anaplasia). WT1 nuclear positivity highlights blastema/epithelium; BCOR/cyclin D1 flags CCSK; INI1 loss flags MRTK.
